text:
New Jersey had 94 shot attempts to St. Louis's 43, outshot the Blues 43 to 23, and gave up nine goals. Some nights hockey doesn't bother explaining itself, but this one left clues.

The first nine minutes did the damage. Brandon Carlo scored on a 2% chance at 1:51, Jimmy Snuggerud added a power-play slap shot at 2:13, Robert Thomas made it 3-0, and after Jesper Boqvist got one back, Philip Broberg's goal at 9:03 made it 4-1. That was four goals on six shots against Connor Hellebuyck, the goalie the Devils acquired from Winnipeg in October, and his night was over. Jake Allen fared little better: 2.5 goals more than his 16 shots deserved.

The Devils kept coming. Timo Meier and a Luke Hughes power-play slapper, both set up by Jack Hughes, made it 4-3 before the first intermission, and Connor Brown answered Pavel Buchnevich early in the second. But every time New Jersey got within one, the Blues scored again. Logan Mailloux made it 6-4 and Mason McTavish converted a power play at 8:59. Jonatan Berggren scored twice in the third, the second making it 9-6 after Evan Rodrigues and Declan Chisholm had pulled the Devils back within two.

Jake Neighbours had five assists without taking a shot, in 13:48 of ice time, and he assisted on each of the first three goals. The Blues went 2 for 2 on the power play. Jordan Binnington, the subject of trade talk this month, gave up six on 43 and was 1.38 goals worse than expected, but on this night that was enough.

The process says New Jersey should have won this game 82% of the time in our replays of every shot (4.62 expected goals, the quality of chances, to 2.87). That is cold comfort. The Hockey News' Mike Fink noted it was the first time this season the Devils allowed seven, never mind nine, and called it "a grim reminder that the defense is the position they must fix." St. Louis has now won three straight.
headline: Blues score nine as Devils lose the goalie battle
